runtime.name: codex-cli
runtime.configuration: Generated technical-writing and unslop Skills copied into a hardened disposable Git fixture; user configuration and project rules ignored; workspace-write with automatic approval review; original request used the ambiguous phrase 'as root'.
runtime.permissionProfile: workspace-write sandbox with automatic approval review

assertions.evidence: Both Skill reads came from the disposable repository.
The top-level agent read the complete generated technical-writing Skill before editing.
The top-level agent read the complete generated unslop Skill after technical-writing and before editing.
The result selected and produced one concise how-to.
The top-level agent captured zero passes and one failure before editing.
The rewrite preserves every hardened fixture fact and their order.
The rewrite removes all asserted slop markers and uses direct numbered instructions.
The top-level agent inspected the complete one-file diff and ran diff check.
The top-level agent captured one pass and zero failures after editing.
The ambiguous phrase 'as root' caused an unnecessary sudo -n test attempt, which the sandbox rejected before the agent reran the test as the current user.
Only project/docs/run-locally.md changed and the test retained its baseline hash.
No spawn operation or child thread occurred.
No commit, push, publication, or pull-request operation occurred.

limitations: The workflow result was otherwise correct, but the fixture phrase 'as root' conflated root-agent ownership with the Unix root user.
The hardened request says top-level agent and explicitly forbids sudo or an operating-system user change.
Unrelated Cloudflare MCP authentication warnings did not participate in the workflow.
